note.text:
Adding in base b works like adding in base ten, but you carry when a column reaches b, not ten.

Example in base 5: 34₅ + 23₅
• Units: 4 + 3 = 7. Seven is one five and 2 more: write 2, carry 1.
• Fives: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6, which is one five and 1 more: write 1, carry 1.
• Write the last carry, 1.
So 34₅ + 23₅ = 112₅.

Subtracting: when the top digit is too small, borrow 1 from the next column. In base b, the 1 you borrow is worth b, not ten.
Example in base 5: 42₅ − 13₅. Units: 2 − 3 is not possible, so borrow: 2 + 5 = 7 and 7 − 3 = 4. Fives: 3 − 1 = 2. Answer: 24₅.

Check in base ten: 34₅ = 19, 23₅ = 13, and 19 + 13 = 32 = 112₅.

steps: Units: {dig(x, 0)} + {dig(y, 0)} = {c0}. That is {k0} group of {b} and {c0 % b} more: write {c0 % b}, carry {k0}.
{b}s column: {dig(x, 1)} + {dig(y, 1)} + {k0} = {c1}. That is {k1} group of {b} and {c1 % b} more: write {c1 % b}, carry {k1}.
{b ^ 2}s column: {dig(x, 2)} + {dig(y, 2)} + {k1} = {c2}. This is less than {b}: write {c2}.
Check in base ten: {x}{sub(b)} = {fromBase(x, b)} and {y}{sub(b)} = {fromBase(y, b)}. {fromBase(x, b)} + {fromBase(y, b)} = {total}, and {total} in base {b} is {toBase(total, b)}{sub(b)}.
checks: str(c2) + str(c1 % b) + str(c0 % b) == toBase(total, b)

cards.idea: In base b there is no digit b. One group of b is written {10}: one b and no units.
Add column by column from the right. When a column reaches b, write what is left over after taking b away, and carry {1}.
example: Units: {dig(x, 0)} + {dig(y, 0)} = {dig(x, 0) + dig(y, 0)} = {b} + {dig(x, 0) + dig(y, 0) - b}: write {dig(x, 0) + dig(y, 0) - b}, carry {1}.
checks: dig(x, 0) + dig(y, 0) >= b && dig(x, 0) + dig(y, 0) < 2 * b
'1' + str(dig(x, 1) + dig(y, 1) + 1 - b) + str(dig(x, 0) + dig(y, 0) - b) == toBase(fromBase(x, b) + fromBase(y, b), b)

misconceptions.explain: {d} + {e} = {d + e} in base ten. That is one group of {b} and {d + e - b} more: {toBase(d + e, b)}{sub(b)}.

solution: {d} + {e} = {d + e} = {b} + {d + e - b}: one group of {b} and {d + e - b} more.

cards.idea: To subtract, start from the right. If the top digit is too small, borrow {1} from the next column: in base b it is worth b.
example: Units: {dig(x, 0)} − {dig(y, 0)} is not possible. Borrow: {dig(x, 0)} + {b} = {dig(x, 0) + b}, and {dig(x, 0) + b} − {dig(y, 0)} = {dig(x, 0) + b - dig(y, 0)}.
checks: str(dig(x, 1) - 1 - dig(y, 1)) + str(dig(x, 0) + b - dig(y, 0)) == toBase(fromBase(x, b) - fromBase(y, b), b)

misconceptions.explain: The 1 you borrow is worth {b} in base {b}, not ten: {p} + {b} − {q} = {b + p - q}.
There is no digit {b} in base {b}. One group of {b} is written 10: one {b} and no units.
{b - 1} + 1 makes one full group of {b}: write 0 in the units and carry 1. That is 10.

solution: {b - 1} + {1} = {b}: one full group of {b} and nothing left over.
In base {b} that is written {toBase(b, b)}: one {b} and {0} units.

questions.prompt: In base {b}, calculate {x}{sub(b)} + {y}{sub(b)}. Give your answer in base {b}.
questions.verify: fromBase(answer, b) == fromBase(x, b) + fromBase(y, b)

misconceptions.explain: In base {b} you carry when a column reaches {b}, not ten.

solution: Check in base ten: {fromBase(x, b)} + {fromBase(y, b)} = {fromBase(x, b) + fromBase(y, b)}.

questions.prompt: In base {b}, calculate {x}{sub(b)} − {y}{sub(b)}. Give your answer in base {b}.
questions.verify: fromBase(answer, b) + fromBase(y, b) == fromBase(x, b)

misconceptions.explain: When you borrow in base {b}, the 1 you borrow is worth {b}, not ten.

solution: Check in base ten: {fromBase(x, b)} − {fromBase(y, b)} = {fromBase(x, b) - fromBase(y, b)}.

questions.where: decAdd(toBase(p4, b), toBase(q4, b)) != toBase(p4 + q4, b)
questions.prompt: Mih did four additions in base {b}. One is wrong. Which one?

right.truth: fromBase(toBase(p1 + q1, b), b) == fromBase(toBase(p1, b), b) + fromBase(toBase(q1, b), b)
fromBase(toBase(p2 + q2, b), b) == fromBase(toBase(p2, b), b) + fromBase(toBase(q2, b), b)
fromBase(toBase(p3 + q3, b), b) == fromBase(toBase(p3, b), b) + fromBase(toBase(q3, b), b)

wrong.truth: fromBase(decAdd(toBase(p4, b), toBase(q4, b)), b) == fromBase(toBase(p4, b), b) + fromBase(toBase(q4, b), b)
wrong.explain: This sum was done with base-ten carrying. In base {b} the answer is {toBase(p4 + q4, b)}{sub(b)}.
